clue.text: Scottish king seen as dull mug

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
a mug and a can are both drinking vessels

explanation.surface: A Scottish monarch is portrayed as a dreary fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a fool or a face; here it is a drinking vessel. Duncan is the king murdered in Shakespeare's Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan was an early king of Scotland, famous as the monarch Macbeth kills.

clue.text: Superior wise person demonstrates customary style of language

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class, superior speech or manners
a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: A learned scholar shows the conventional way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class (as in 'U and non-U' English) is a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means the established, habitual way words are employed in a language.

clue.text: Gloomy church always getting smaller in number

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
less means a smaller amount or number

explanation.surface: A congregation keeps shrinking, leaving the church a dismal place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without cheer is dismal, so the word is a synonym for gloomy.

clue.text: Something sweet making aunt go crazy

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A treat that sends an aunt wild with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Maiden, one facing emotional pressure as 'the other woman'?

parts.note: M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over
the Roman numeral for one is I
stress is emotional or mental pressure

explanation.surface: A young woman under strain finds herself cast as a married man's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman, but it is the cricket term: an over with no runs scored, M on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistress is a married man's lover, commonly called the other woman in an affair.

clue.text: Variation by mule — this being awkward?

definitions.text: Variation by mule — this being awkward?

indicators.note: being awkward means the letters behave contrarily, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stubborn mule, being awkward, is hard to steer: that is what it lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words before 'being awkward' are rearranged; the whole clue then describes the quality a balky mule shows a want of.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means ease of steering or handling, which an awkward, contrary mule notably lacks.

clue.text: Go across step half missing on rickety ladder

indicators.note: with half missing, only the front two of the four letters of step remain
rickety means shaky and unstable, so the letters of ladder are jumbled

explanation.surface: A climber reaches across a gap where a rung is gone on a wobbly ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go across' reads as a command, but it is the definition; 'rickety' gives RADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to extend across or span something, with a part on each side.

clue.text: Field with only half the Spanish football team

indicators.note: only half of the ten-letter club name is kept, its front portion

parts.note: Real Madrid is the famous Spanish football club

explanation.surface: A pitch occupied by just half of a Spanish side.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten letters halved leave five: the front half of REAL MADRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a sphere or domain of activity, as is a field of study or work.

clue.text: Thus male has no time for self-denial, being languid

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
Lent is the forty-day Christian season of fasting and self-denial

explanation.surface: A man too lethargic to bother with abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy and sluggish, close in sense to languid and listless.

clue.text: Wild ape, grunter in exciting tale

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wild, snorting ape stars in a thrilling story.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping book makes the reader keep flipping onward, hence the compound name for a thriller.

clue.text: A modern miss collecting pounds for charity

indicators.note: collecting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ms is the modern title for a woman, replacing Miss or Mrs
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A young woman gathers money for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' puts L inside MS, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts of money or food to the poor, an old word for charity.

clue.text: Free from grime when brought into class

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a degree is a class or grade of rank
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Cleaning off dirt once taken into a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrease is to strip oil and grime from something, i.e. to clean it.

clue.text: Numbers crazy about fruit

indicators.note: about signals a turn, so the combined letters run backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Someone is obsessed with fruit figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NOSMAD. 'Crazy about' looks like 'keen on', but 'about' works alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark-purple plum, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Think as timid type that's lost love

indicators.note: that's lost means a piece has gone missing from the word before

parts.note: a mouse is a timid, shy person
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A shy person broods after a romance ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O comes from the tennis score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or reflect, so it is a synonym for think.

clue.text: As one outside home, very unlike welcome guest

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the first piece wraps the others

parts.note: united means acting as one
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone left out of the house is quite unlike the guest everyone wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As one' reads as part of the picture, but it is the word for joined together, which goes round the home and very letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome guest has been asked; someone not asked turns up without a request.

clue.text: Community member, mostly horrible, wanting drink in pub?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: vile means horrible
lager is a beer drunk in pubs

explanation.surface: A local, rather nasty, craves a pint at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A villager is a resident of a village, one member of that small community.

clue.text: Possibly a sugar, not something bitter

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A sweet sugar turns out to be bitter instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura bitters are an aromatic flavouring used in cocktails such as pink gin.

clue.text: One opposed gets to induce scorn

parts.note: a con is an argument or person against, as in pros and cons
to tempt is to entice or induce

explanation.surface: An opponent gets to provoke derision.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and scorn both mean disdain for something judged worthless.

clue.text: Displaced people creating ado with Paris wrecked

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fuss as the French capital is ruined, leaving refugees.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people scattered from their homeland, such as an exiled population.

clue.text: Things that can kill animal in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a stag is an animal, a male deer

explanation.surface: Lethal weapons trained on a fleeing beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Gat is old American slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gats are handguns in gangster slang, and firearms can be lethal.

clue.text: Having a position in power, subsequently lambasted

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
laced means beaten or thrashed, as in a lacing

explanation.surface: Someone in office who was then attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put somewhere has been located or set in a spot, so it has a position.

clue.text: Bird, old and cold, grasped by an animal doctor

parts.note: an gives the article A

indicators.note: grasped by means held inside, so those letters go within the other piece

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An elderly, chilled bird is held by a veterinary surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasped by' puts OC between AV and ET.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Piece of poetry from somewhere in Switzerland, unfinished?

indicators.note: unfinished means the end is not done, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a canton is one of the regions Switzerland is divided into

explanation.surface: A poem composed somewhere in the Alps, left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a major division of a long poem, as in Dante's Inferno.

clue.text: I exist concealing endless desire, one appearing to be unreal

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to live is to exist

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: Someone hides their longing yet seems not quite real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes the final letter off the desire word before it hides inside the existence word.
explanation.definitionFit: Illusive describes what deceives the senses, an illusion that seems real but is not.

clue.text: Call and sink into chair maybe after six

indicators.note: after tells us the sitting piece comes behind the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to sit is to sink into a chair, for example

explanation.surface: Pay a call and slump into an armchair after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like a phone call or a shout; it is the definition, a short stay with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to pay them a short visit.

clue.text: English people of fashion in college

parts.note: the ton is an old word for fashionable society

explanation.surface: Stylish English folk at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is the English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is the famous boarding school whose full name is Eton College.

clue.text: Direction taken by sailor? One makes a bit of a meal of it!

definitions.meaning: the main is the open sea, and a course is the heading a sailor steers

definitions.text: One makes a bit of a meal of it
definitions.meaning: the principal dish is one part of a full meal

explanation.surface: A seafarer's heading, and a quip about making a meal of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a meal of it' means overdoing something; here it is literal, one dish of several.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit: a heading over the open sea, and the chief dish of a dinner.

clue.text: New tiro, learner within day working with skill

indicators.note: within means inside, so the second group goes into the first
working means being worked over, so the letters of day are reordered
new means made afresh, so the letters of tiro are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner sign on cars

explanation.surface: A novice learner driver, on the job one day, does it deftly.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals: 'New' makes ROIT, and 'working' makes ADY, which takes ROIT plus L between its D and Y. 'working with skill' tempts as the definition, but 'working' is busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something adroitly means doing it cleverly and deftly.

clue.text: Planet faced with onset of deadly shortage?

indicators.note: onset of means the beginning, so take the opening letter

parts.note: Earth is a planet

explanation.surface: A world confronted by the start of a lethal scarcity.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something.
